newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina arrests six in smuggling crackdown.
newsitem.headline: Argentina arrests six in smuggling crackdown.

text.p: Argentine authorities said on Thursday they arrested six people and are searching for others in connection with a ring that smuggled in 40 metric tons of cameras, surgical instruments, perfume and electronics from the United States this year.
Prosecutor Emilio Guerberoff told Reuters police "arrested six people and 18 are on the run" who are suspected of smuggling the goods between February and October of this year.
All the detainees are Argentine nationals -- including two Air Force officers, a pilot and a civilian member of the Air Force -- and the fugitives include Uruguayans.

Guerberoff said Argentine authorities have asked Interpol to help them track down the foreign suspects. He said he had no indication so far of any U.S. citizens being involved in the smuggling ring, but "we are not ruling that out."
Guerberoff said the smuggled goods, which also included computers and clothing, arrived at Buenos Aires' Ezeiza international airport from New York and Miami on commercial airliners.

But instead of being unloaded, the cargo was reshipped to Uruguay's Carrasco airport, where it was marked as being in transit, the prosecutor said. From Carrasco, the contraband was re-embarked in air taxis and shipped back to Ezeiza -- dodging the stricter controls normally applied to big airliners' cargo.
Guerberoff said he suspected the smuggled goods were sneaked out of Ezeiza airport through holes in the fence around the terminal.
Smuggling and racketeering convictions carry prison sentences of up to five years.
The case adds to a host of charges of corruption in the customs service, which the government estimates has cost it some $3 billion in lost customs duties in the past few years.

In November President Carlos Menem's administration announced a crackdown on graft in the customs service, which included the firing of all customs staff at Ezeiza airport and the appointment of a new administrator.
